unitTitle: Present Perfect Simple - Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple - Present Perfect Continuous

pairsWith.noteUz: Present Perfect vaqt so'zlari, have gone/have been, Past Simple bilan farqi, Present Perfect Continuous nazariyasi.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 7-UNIT NAZARIYA DAVOMI (35-bet, PDF 34). Yuqorida o'ngda ko'k '7'. Och pushti ramka.

• We use for to express duration. 'I have known Sue for ten years.' • We use since to state a starting point. 'She hasn't been to New York since 1992.' • We use just and already in affirmative sentences. 'She's already booked a table for two. I've just bought a new dress.' • We use yet in questions and negations. 'Has Jim fixed the car yet? They haven't cooked dinner yet.'
'Have gone (to) - Have been (to)': There are two ways to form the present perfect of the verb go: have gone and have been, but there is a difference in meaning. Study the examples below: 'Thomas and Anne have gone to Lisbon. (They went to Lisbon some time ago and they are still there.) I have been to Lisbon. (I have visited Lisbon and have come back. I am not there now.)'
'Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple': • We use the past simple for an action which happened at a stated time in the past or for an action which started and finished in the past. 'Fred graduated from university in 1997. Pauline went to the dentist three days ago.' • We use the present perfect simple for an action which happened at an unstated time in the past or for an action which started in the past and is still continuing in the present. 'Carol has joined the tennis club. He has been a teacher for twenty years.'
'Present Perfect Continuous' JADVALI: Affirmative - Long form: I have been doing, you have been doing, he has been doing, she has been doing, it has been doing, we have been doing, you have been doing, they have been doing; Short form: I've been doing, you've been doing, he's been doing ... Interrogative: Have I been doing? Have you been doing? Has he been doing? ... Negative - Long form: I have not been doing ...; Short form: I haven't been doing, he hasn't been doing ...
'Form': • We form the present perfect continuous with the auxiliary verb have/has, the past participle of the verb to be (been) and the main verb with the -ing. 'I have been working. She has been sleeping.' • We form questions by putting have/has before the subject. 'Have they been playing?' • We form negations by putting not between have/has and been. 'She has not/hasn't been reading.'
'Use': We use the present perfect continuous for: • an action which started in the past and continues up to the present. 'She has been typing letters for three hours.' • an action which has recently finished and its result is evident now. 'They are tired. They have been working for nine hours.'
'Time Expressions used with the present perfect continuous': for, since, all morning/afternoon/week/day, etc.

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '35'.

sections.titleUz: Present Perfect - vaqt so'zlari / Have gone - Have been

exercises.instructionEn: We use for to express duration: I have known Sue for ten years. We use since to state a starting point: She hasn't been to New York since 1992. We use just and already in affirmative sentences: She's already booked a table for two. I've just bought a new dress. We use yet in questions and negations: Has Jim fixed the car yet? They haven't cooked dinner yet. Have gone (to) - Have been (to): Thomas and Anne have gone to Lisbon. (They went to Lisbon some time ago and they are still there.) I have been to Lisbon. (I have visited Lisbon and have come back. I am not there now.)
exercises.instructionUz: 'For' - davomiylik (muddat) uchun: Men Syuni o'n yildan beri bilaman. 'Since' - boshlanish nuqtasi uchun: U 1992-yildan beri Nyu-Yorkda bo'lmagan. 'Just' va 'already' tasdiq gaplarda: U allaqachon ikki kishilik stol band qilgan. Men endigina yangi ko'ylak sotib oldim. 'Yet' savol va inkorda: Jim mashinani tuzatdimi hali? Ular hali ovqat pishirishmagan. Have gone (to) - Have been (to): Tomas va Enn Lissabonga ketishgan. (Ular bir muncha vaqt oldin ketgan va hali o'sha yerda.) Men Lissabonda bo'lganman. (Men Lissabonni ziyorat qilib qaytganman. Hozir u yerda emasman.)
exercises.explanationUz:
VAQT SO'ZLARI - QAYERDA, QAChON?

  FOR + MUDDAT (qancha vaqt):
    for ten years, for three hours
    I have known Sue FOR ten years.

  SINCE + NUQTA (qachondan):
    since 1992, since Monday
    She hasn't been to New York
    SINCE 1992.

  JUST (endigina) va ALREADY
  (allaqachon) - TASDIQDA, have va
  V3 orasida:
    She's ALREADY booked a table.
    I've JUST bought a new dress.

  YET (hali) - SAVOL va INKORDA,
  gap OXIRIDA:
    Has Jim fixed the car YET?
    They haven't cooked dinner YET.


HAVE GONE va HAVE BEEN:

  HAVE GONE TO = ketgan (hali
    o'sha yerda):
    Thomas and Anne HAVE GONE TO
    Lisbon. (hali Lissabonda)

  HAVE BEEN TO = bo'lgan (borib
    qaytgan):
    I HAVE BEEN TO Lisbon. (hozir
    bu yerdaman)

She's already booked a table for two. I've just bought a new dress. (just, already - affirmative)

points.en: Has Jim fixed the car yet? They haven't cooked dinner yet. (yet - questions and negations)
points.uz: Jim mashinani tuzatdimi hali? Ular hali ovqat pishirishmagan. (savol va inkorda)

sections.title: Past Simple vs Present Perfect Simple
sections.titleUz: Past Simple va Present Perfect Simple farqi

exercises.instructionEn: We use the past simple for an action which happened at a stated time in the past or for an action which started and finished in the past: Fred graduated from university in 1997. Pauline went to the dentist three days ago. We use the present perfect simple for an action which happened at an unstated time in the past or for an action which started in the past and is still continuing in the present: Carol has joined the tennis club. He has been a teacher for twenty years.
exercises.instructionUz: Past simple - o'tmishda ANIQ VAQTDA bo'lgan yoki o'tmishda boshlanib TUGAGAN harakat uchun: Fred universitetni 1997-yilda bitirgan. Polin uch kun oldin tish shifokoriga bordi. Present perfect simple - o'tmishda NOMA'LUM VAQTDA bo'lgan yoki o'tmishda boshlanib HOZIR HAM DAVOM ETAYOTGAN harakat uchun: Kerol tennis klubiga qo'shilgan. U yigirma yildan beri o'qituvchi.
exercises.explanationUz:
PAST SIMPLE yoki PRESENT PERFECT?

  PAST SIMPLE - ANIQ VAQT / TUGAGAN:
    Fred GRADUATED in 1997. (qachon
    - aniq)
    Pauline WENT to the dentist
    three days ago. (ago - tugagan)

  PRESENT PERFECT - NOMA'LUM VAQT /
  HOZIR HAM DAVOM:
    Carol HAS JOINED the tennis
    club. (qachon - aytilmaydi)
    He HAS BEEN a teacher for
    twenty years. (hozir ham
    o'qituvchi)


⚠ KALIT SO'ZLAR:

  in 1997, ago, yesterday, last
  week → PAST SIMPLE
  for, since, just, already, yet,
  ever → PRESENT PERFECT


⚠ 'HE WAS A TEACHER FOR 20 YEARS'
  = endi emas (Past Simple)
  'HE HAS BEEN A TEACHER FOR 20
  YEARS' = hozir ham (Perfect)

points.en: Fred graduated from university in 1997. Pauline went to the dentist three days ago. (past simple: stated time / finished)
points.uz: Fred universitetni 1997-yilda bitirgan. Polin uch kun oldin tish shifokoriga bordi. (aniq vaqt)

points.en: Carol has joined the tennis club. He has been a teacher for twenty years. (present perfect: unstated time / still continuing)
points.uz: Kerol tennis klubiga qo'shilgan. U yigirma yildan beri o'qituvchi. (noma'lum vaqt / davom)

exercises.instructionEn: Affirmative: I/you/we/they have been doing (I've been doing), he/she/it has been doing (he's been doing). Interrogative: Have I been doing? Has he been doing? Negative: I haven't been doing, he hasn't been doing. Form: have/has + been + main verb -ing: I have been working. She has been sleeping. Questions: Have they been playing? Negations: She has not/hasn't been reading. Use: an action which started in the past and continues up to the present: She has been typing letters for three hours; an action which has recently finished and its result is evident now: They are tired. They have been working for nine hours. Time expressions: for, since, all morning/afternoon/week/day, etc.
exercises.instructionUz: Tasdiq: I/you/we/they have been doing (I've been doing), he/she/it has been doing (he's been doing). So'roq: Have I been doing? Has he been doing? Inkor: I haven't been doing, he hasn't been doing. Shakl: have/has + been + asosiy fe'l-ing: Men ishlab kelyapman. U uxlab yotibdi. Savol: Have they been playing? Inkor: She hasn't been reading. Ishlatilishi: o'tmishda boshlanib HOZIRGAChA DAVOM ETAYOTGAN harakat: U uch soatdan beri xat yozyapti; YAQINDA TUGAGAN va natijasi hozir ko'rinib turgan harakat: Ular charchagan. Ular to'qqiz soat ishlashdi. Vaqt so'zlari: for, since, all morning/afternoon/week/day va h.k.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS =
  HAVE / HAS + BEEN + FE'L-ING.

  TASDIQ: I HAVE BEEN working. She
    HAS BEEN sleeping.
  SO'ROQ: HAVE they BEEN playing?
  INKOR: She HASN'T BEEN reading.


QAChON:

  1) O'TMIShDAN HOZIRGAChA DAVOM
     (jarayon urg'ulanadi):
     She HAS BEEN TYPING letters
     FOR three hours. (hali
     yozyapti)

  2) YAQINDA TUGAGAN, NATIJASI
     KO'RINIB TURIBDI:
     They are tired. They HAVE
     BEEN WORKING for nine hours.
     (charchagan - chunki uzoq
     ishladi)


VAQT SO'ZLARI:

  for, since, all morning / all
  day / all week


⚠ SIMPLE va CONTINUOUS FARQI:

  I have painted the kitchen.
  (natija - bo'yalgan, tugadi)
  I have been painting the
  kitchen. (jarayon - shu bilan
  band edim, balki tugamagan)


⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  '-yapti' + 'dan beri': 'uch
  soatdan beri yozyapti'.

points.en: I have been working. She has been sleeping. — Have they been playing? — She hasn't been reading.
She has been typing letters for three hours. (started in the past, continues up to the present)
points.uz: U uch soatdan beri xat yozyapti. (hozirgacha davom)

points.en: They are tired. They have been working for nine hours. (recently finished, result evident now)
points.uz: Ular charchagan. Ular to'qqiz soat ishlashdi. (natija ko'rinib turibdi)

points.en: for, since, all morning / afternoon / week / day

patterns.formula: KIM + has / have + already / just + V3 — Has + KIM + V3 + yet?
patterns.exampleEn: She's already booked a table. I've just bought a new dress. Has Jim fixed the car yet?
patterns.exampleUz: U allaqachon stol band qilgan. Endigina ko'ylak sotib oldim. Jim mashinani tuzatdimi hali?

patterns.formula: KIM + has gone to + JOY (hali o'sha yerda) / KIM + has been to + JOY (qaytgan)
patterns.exampleEn: Thomas and Anne have gone to Lisbon. I have been to Lisbon.
patterns.exampleUz: Tomas va Enn Lissabonga ketishgan. Men Lissabonda bo'lganman.

patterns.formula: KIM + V2 + in 1997 / ago (Past Simple) — KIM + has V3 + for/since (Present Perfect)
patterns.exampleEn: Fred graduated in 1997. He has been a teacher for twenty years.
patterns.exampleUz: Fred 1997-yilda bitirgan. U yigirma yildan beri o'qituvchi.

patterns.formula: KIM + has / have been + V-ing + for + MUDDAT
patterns.exampleEn: She has been typing letters for three hours.
patterns.exampleUz: U uch soatdan beri xat yozyapti.
